Realty Income (NYSE: O), The Monthly Dividend Company®, is real estate partner to the world's leading companies®. We invest in people and places to deliver dependable monthly dividends that increase over time. The company is structured as a real estate investment trust (\"REIT\"), and its monthly dividends are supported by the cash flow from over 15,500 real estate properties primarily owned under long-term net lease agreements with commercial clients. The company has declared more than 650 consecutive monthly dividends on its shares of common stock and is a member of the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats® index for having increased the dividend for over 31 consecutive years. \n\nAdditional information about the company can be found at www.realtyincome.com. Founded in 1969. It has 722 employees. Annual revenue is $5.7B. IPO 1994.\n\n# Transcript\n\n**Operator**\n\nGood day, and welcome to the Realty Income third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. We've expanded the levers available to us across both investment and capital formation, broadening where we can invest and how we can fund those investments. Few companies in our sector have the same ability to mobilize capital across geographies, asset types, investment structures, and funding sources in an increasingly fluid market environment. We saw the benefit of those capabilities again in our third quarter results, with AFFO per share of $1.12, representing growth of 3.7% YoY, alongside continued strength across our operating portfolio. Based on our performance and outlook, we are raising our 2026 AFFO per share guidance to $4.45-$4.46, while reaffirming our $10 billion investment volume target. During the quarter, we invested approximately $2.6 billion, including $2.2 billion at our pro rata share, with a cash yield of 6.8%, and for property acquisitions, weighted average annual contractual rent increases of 1.9%. Importantly, those investments had a realized leverage-neutral spread of approximately 170 basis points to our short-term weighted average cost of capital, and 53% of investment activity was with investment-grade clients. We sourced a record of approximately $59 billion of potential investments during the quarter, bringing year-to-date sourcing to more than $120 billion, already surpassing our prior full-year record. Higher long-term interest rates have shifted the most attractive investment economics towards Europe, credit investments, and private capital managed co-investments. These channels provide ways to enhance our investment spreads and create additional avenues to deploy capital when rate volatility pressures balance sheet acquisition economics. Against that backdrop, Europe stands out as an area of particularly attractive relative value. Based on our performance and outlook, we are raising our 2026 AFFO per share guidance to $4.45-$4.46, while reaffirming our $10 billion investment volume target. During the quarter, we invested approximately $2.6 billion, including $2.2 billion at our pro rata share, with a cash yield of 6.8%, and for property acquisitions, weighted average annual contractual rent increases of 1.9%. Importantly, those investments had a realized leverage-neutral spread of approximately 170 basis points to our short-term weighted average cost of capital, and 53% of investment activity was with investment-grade clients. We sourced a record of approximately $59 billion of potential investments during the quarter, bringing year-to-date sourcing to more than $120 billion, already surpassing our prior full-year record. This activity represented a 4.4% selectivity rate, with 92% of our investment activity being relationship-driven. Jonathan will provide details on the financing that supported these investments. Our results demonstrate the value of having multiple investment and capital levers as relative economics change. Higher long-term interest rates have shifted the most attractive investment economics towards Europe, credit investments, and private capital managed co-investments. These channels provide ways to enhance our investment spreads and create additional avenues to deploy capital when rate volatility pressures balance sheet acquisition economics. Against that backdrop, Europe stands out as an area of particularly attractive relative value. During the third quarter, we invested approximately $940 million in Europe, representing 42% of pro rata investment volume at an initial weighted average cash yield of 7.1%. More than 85% of our European real estate investment volume was industrial, at an initial cash yield of 6.9%. One of our largest investments during the quarter was a $180 million e-commerce logistics facility in western Poland, leased to a large investment-grade international retailer at a 6.8% yield. The recently constructed purpose-built facility sits within an established logistics hub and supports product distribution across Central and Western Europe. It is representative of the industrial opportunities we are pursuing in Europe, modern purpose-built assets within established logistics markets that serve broad regional demand. While price discovery continues to evolve in light of the higher rate environment, we remain constructive on continental Europe heading into the balance of the year, with opportunities emerging through existing relationships and across multiple markets. Our advantage is not simply geographic reach. It is the local teams, relationships, and playbook we have built to evaluate Europe market by market and act when the economics meet our standards. In addition to broadening our capital sources, we have expanded the ways we can invest across the capital structure. During the third quarter, we invested approximately $250 million in credit investments, representing over 10% of total volume across retail, industrial, and data centers. Credit investments represent a compelling way to pivot capital toward superior risk-adjusted returns in response to a high-rate environment. Our credit investment strategy draws on the same discipline and real estate expertise that underpin our equity investments, with a focus on high-quality real estate collateral, strong counterparties, and attractive positioning in the capital stack. These investments are in industries and assets that are already prevalent throughout our real estate portfolio and with partners who are leaders in their respective industries. Importantly, the higher yields available through credit can also serve as a natural hedge to the higher financing costs we incur in a higher rate environment, further strengthening the reliability of the cash flows our business produces. We approach these investments through a real estate lens. Credit can deepen our understanding of operators and the underlying real estate across both the U.S. and Europe, while facilitating a potential path to future ownership and strengthening our relationships with key market participants. Credit is not a substitute for traditional real estate. It is a complement and another lever we can use when the risk-adjusted returns are more compelling, as they are today. Industrial offers a combination of industry tailwinds and embedded growth. It was our largest area of investment during the quarter, with approximately $1.15 billion invested at an initial weighted average cash yield of 6.5%, with weighted average contractual rent increases of 2.5% domestically and international leases largely tied to inflation and market rent growth. Across e-commerce, manufacturing, digital infrastructure, adjacent uses, and a growing range of industrial real estate client use cases, we are finding opportunities supported by durable demand. Those fundamentals are also reflected in increasing build-to-suit activity, repeat demand from existing customers, and significant contractual rent growth. Dallas industrial fundamentals remain very strong, supported by substantial net absorption that continues to outpace new supply and drive vacancy lower. During the third quarter, we acquired a large logistics park adjacent to DFW Airport. The acquired portfolio has in place rents that are approximately 45% below market, creating meaningful mark-to-market growth potential as leases begin to roll in a few years. Data centers also remain part of our long-term investment strategy, but we are staying selective. We are focused on top-tier supply constraint markets, experienced operators, established clients with long-duration leases, and strong annual lease escalators, and real estate where we have conviction in the long-term residual value. Lastly, an increasingly important part of our capital allocation strategy is using our current portfolio as a source of funding. During the third quarter, we completed approximately $527 million of dispositions, including occupied sales of $395 million at a 7.1% net cap rate. We expect disposition activity to remain elevated in the fourth quarter. Year-to-date, disposition proceeds have reached approximately $875 million, already exceeding our full year 2025 disposition volume on the heels of a more proactive capital recycling program. Importantly, our disposition strategy is not just about reducing portfolio risk. We are also selling well-performing assets when the private market value and reinvestment returns create a better outcome. Our objective is to generate non-dilutive capital that can be redeployed toward investments offering superior risk-adjusted returns. Stepping back, we have broadened both sides of capital allocation, where we can invest and how we fund those investments. That adaptability matters because the best use of capital will change over time. Our focus remains on using the breadth of the business to stay selective, pursue the best risk-adjusted returns, and act with conviction as market conditions evolve. With that, I will turn the call over to Jonathan.\n\n...\n\nAs Sumit noted, we completed approximately $2.2 billion of pro rata investment activity during the quarter at an initial weighted average cash yield of approximately 6.8%. Based on the actual financing activity we executed upon over the quarter, we financed these investments with a blended year-one cost of capital of approximately 5%. As a result, we generated a leverage-neutral investment spread of approximately 170 basis points. These economics reflect a deliberate effort to broaden how we finance the business so that our investment decisions are not dependent on the attractiveness of any single capital source. As relative costs and market conditions evolve, the ability to toggle through a variety of alternatives allows us to preserve investment spreads while maintaining our leverage discipline. We put that approach into practice during the quarter by accessing both the euro-denominated debt and convertible markets. In July, we issued EUR 600 million of senior unsecured notes at an effective annual yield of approximately 3.7%, drawing on the depth and lower yield of the euro market. In August, we returned to the convertible market for the second time this year, issuing $1 billion of 3.75% convertible senior notes and generating approximately $950 million in net proceeds after purchasing a capped call that locked in an effective conversion price of $83.55 per share, up 35% from the reference price in August and up approximately 45% from today's closing price. ... Clearly, the breadth of our capital alternatives has allowed us to be less dependent on the ATM equity market. Specifically, public equity funded only 19% of pro rata investment volume year-to-date, compared with an annual average of 47% over the prior three years. An important part of that evolution is our increasing access to private capital, where the recently closed KKR joint venture extends our retirement and insurance private capital strategy to a new partner and geography. As part of the partnership, KKR invested EUR 528 million for a 49% equity interest in a portfolio of 54 retail and industrial assets across four European countries at a 5.9% initial cap rate, including recurring asset management fees. The structure of the joint venture gives Realty Income the ability to call KKR's interest between years 10 and 17 of the joint venture to effectuate a 6.4% IRR, which represents a highly attractive long-term cost of equity with a partner that values the long duration, consistent cash flow characteristics of a diversified net lease portfolio. The strategic significance extends beyond the capital raise in this transaction. By pairing long-term institutional equity with our sourcing, underwriting, and asset management expertise, we are able to leverage our leading net lease operating platform and generate recurring capital asset management fees, expand our buy box of investment opportunities, and minimize share dilution through fewer public equity issuances. Alongside these external ... Together, these funding sources have enabled us to address a substantial portion of our remaining funding needs for 2026 while still preserving significant liquidity and conservative leverage supporting our A-rated balance sheet. Turning to guidance, we are increasing our 2026 AFFO per share guidance by $0.01 at the midpoint and reaffirming our $10 billion investment volume target. We are also increasing our occupancy guidance to above 98.5%, reducing our non-reimbursable expense leakage guidance by 10 basis points at the midpoint to a range of 1.3%-1.5%, and lowering our expectation for credit loss from 40 basis points to approximately 30 basis points. These changes reflect strong asset management execution and better-than-expected tenant credit. We also continue to see a healthy volume and yield outlook for fourth quarter investment activity, which is fully pre-funded from an equity perspective and meaningfully accretive investment spreads. As we look toward 2027, the importance of this expanded funding strategy is not simply that we have more sources of capital, but that we can adapt our financing as relative economics change. We also see an opportunity to build on existing programmatic and strategic relationships and develop new ones with well-respected institutional investors who allocate meaningful capital to net lease strategies outside of the public market. We look forward to sharing our progress as our private capital platform continues to scale. With that, I'll turn the call back to Sumit."],"summary":"Summary:\n- Realty Income (O) reports Q3 2026 results showing a diversified capital allocator strategy across geographies, asset types, and funding sources to improve investment spreads and funding flexibility in a higher-rate environment.\n- AFFO per share: $1.12, up 3.7% YoY. | The Motley Fool\n\n# Why Isn't Realty Income's Stock Taking Off After Strong Earnings Results?\n\nRealty Income delivered another solid quarter, but its results also help explain why the dividend stock hasn't taken off.\n\nBy Matt DiLallo – Nov 3, 2026 at 12:47PM EST\n\n## Key Points\n\n- Realty Income delivered strong third-quarter results, with high occupancy and rising AFFO per share.\n- Despite its growing real estate portfolio, AFFO per share increased only 3.7%, highlighting the challenges of delivering faster growth at its scale.\n- With a dividend yield around 5.6%, Realty Income remains an attractive income investment, even if its stock doesn't take off.\n\nRealty Income (O -0.77%) continues to deliver the results investors expect from one of the world's largest real estate investment trusts (REITs). Its properties remain nearly fully occupied, its dividend is well covered, and its investment program continues to generate attractive returns.\n\nHowever, despite another solid earnings report, the stock hasn't generated much excitement. The reason has less to do with the company's real estate portfolio and more to do with how quickly it can grow earnings per share.\n\nImage source: The Motley Fool.\n\n## Realty Income delivered another solid quarter\n\nRealty Income just keeps getting it done. The REIT grew its adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) by 3.7% in the third quarter to $1.12 per share. That put its dividend payout ratio at a conservative 72.6% of its AFFO, despite continued dividend growth. It has now delivered 5% AFFO per share growth through the first nine months of this year compared to the prior-year period. Its existing real estate portfolio continues to provide steadily rising cash flow. Occupancy was 98.8% at the end of the third quarter, while its rent recapture rate was 103.5% (meaning new leases on the same property were, on average, 3.5% above prior rates). \n\nMeanwhile, the REIT continues to find attractive investment opportunities. It invested another $2.6 billion during the quarter at an initial cash yield of 6.8%. That includes properties acquired in its U.S. Core Fund and through joint ventures, such as its recently established strategic joint venture with KKR in Europe. \n\nThe company remains on pace to invest $10 billion this year. That supports its guidance to deliver $4.45-$4.46 per share of AFFO this year, a $0.01-per-share increase from its prior range. That's a more than 4% increase from last year despite headwinds from higher interest rates. \n\n## O - Realty Income\n\n$59.04-$0.46 (-0.77%)\n\nNYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/06/26\n\n### Key data points\n\nMarket cap Market cap calculation methodology Market cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. That's likely due to three factors.\n\nRealty Income's growth remains modest. AFFO per share grew just 3.7% despite a 10.3% increase in total revenue. Meanwhile, it only increased its full-year guidance by $0.01 per share at both ends of the range. Due to its large scale and net-lease focus, the REIT isn't growing as quickly as others in the industry. \n\nIt also continues to face some headwinds from interest rates. Higher rates increase interest expenses when refinancing existing debt and also drive up borrowing costs for new investments. That's a headwind for AFFO per share growth. Higher rates also weigh on the value of commercial real estate. Realty Income's share price has fallen almost 15% from its peak earlier this year, coinciding with the recent spike in the 10-year Treasury rate. \n\nGiven its size, Realty Income requires significant external capital to fund its investment program. Even highly attractive acquisitions can have a modest effect on AFFO per share when accounting for financing costs.\n\nRealty Income isn't going to grow fast, which is why we shouldn't expect its stock to surge, even with a solid earnings report.\n\n## A compelling dividend stock, but not necessarily a high-growth investment\n\nThe thing with Realty Income is that investors don't need rapid growth to earn an attractive return. At its recent share price of around $57.50, the REIT offers a 5.6% yield at its current monthly dividend rate. It would only need to grow its AFFO per share by around a 4% annual rate to produce an average annualized total return approaching double digits. That assumes no change in its valuation multiple, which is currently a very reasonable 12.9 times. \n\nMeanwhile, there's the potential for additional upside. Realty Income raised its 2026 AFFO guidance to $4.45 to $4.46 per share and reaffirmed its $10 billion investment-volume target.\n\n## Investment activity shifts toward Europe, industrial and credit\n\n Realty Income invested about $2.6 billion during the quarter, or $2.2 billion at its pro rata share, at an initial weighted-average cash yield of 6.8%. Property acquisitions included weighted-average annual contractual rent increases of 1.9%. The company said its investments generated a leverage-neutral spread of about 170 basis points over its short-term weighted-average cost of capital, and 53% of quarterly activity involved investment-grade clients.\n\nThe company sourced a record approximately $59 billion of potential investments during the quarter, bringing year-to-date sourcing above $120 billion. Realty Income completed investments equal to 4.4% of sourced opportunities, while 92% of its activity was relationship-driven.\n\nEurope accounted for approximately $940 million, or 42%, of pro rata investment volume during the quarter, at a 7.1% initial weighted-average cash yield. More than 85% of European real estate investment volume was industrial, with a 6.9% initial cash yield.\n\nAmong its larger European transactions, Realty Income acquired a $180 million e-commerce logistics facility in western Poland, leased to an unnamed investment-grade international retailer. The asset, located in an established logistics hub, was acquired at a 6.8% yield and supports distribution across Central and Western Europe.\n\nIndustrial was the company’s largest investment category overall, with approximately $1.15 billion invested at an initial weighted-average cash yield of 6.5%. Domestic industrial leases carried weighted-average contractual rent increases of 2.5%, while international leases were generally linked to inflation and market rent growth.\n\nRoy also highlighted a logistics-park acquisition near Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. The portfolio’s in-place rents are approximately 45% below market, and Neil Abraham, chief strategy officer and president of Realty Income International, said the company expects to achieve all of that mark-to-market opportunity within the next three and a half years.\n\nIn addition, Realty Income invested approximately $250 million in credit investments across retail, industrial and data centers, representing more than 10% of total quarterly volume. Roy said the credit strategy is designed to complement—not replace—traditional real estate ownership by providing exposure to high-quality collateral and established counterparties at higher yields. The credit investments made in the third quarter had an average duration of approximately 3.4 years.\n\n## Financing strategy supports investment spreads\n\nChief Financial Officer and Treasurer Jonathan Pong said Realty Income ended the quarter with approximately $5.4 billion of available liquidity and net debt to annualized pro forma adjusted EBITDAre of 5.4 times, or 5.2 times including $1.1 billion of unsettled at-the-market equity raised at a weighted-average gross price of $60.61 per share.\n\nMore than 94% of the company’s pro rata debt was fixed rate. Realty Income financed its quarterly investments at a blended year-one cost of capital of approximately 5%, compared with the 6.8% investment yield.\n\nDuring the quarter, Realty Income issued €600 million of senior unsecured notes at an effective annual yield of about 3.7%. It also issued $1 billion of 3.75% convertible senior notes, producing approximately $950 million in net proceeds after the purchase of a capped call. The capped call established an effective conversion price of $83.55 per share, according to Pong.\n\nPublic equity was a smaller component of funding than in prior years. Realty Income settled approximately $470 million through its at-the-market program during the quarter, and public equity represented 19% of pro rata investment volume year to date, compared with an annual average of 47% over the preceding three years.\n\nPong said the company’s access to euro-denominated debt gives it an advantage in funding European acquisitions. He noted that a 10-year fixed-rate unsecured borrowing in euros was approximately 80 basis points less expensive than comparable U.S. dollar debt at the time of the call.\n\n## KKR joint venture and asset sales add","highlights":["pro rata share, at an initial weighted-average cash yield of 6.8%.
